messages:
Amal: quick idea — propose we rescope the UI edge into a tiny projection service that returns panel-shaped payloads and a thin query fanout. move tenant-level RBAC filtering into the projection to reduce per-panel fanout. thoughts?

Tess: curious about perf tradeoffs — won't duplicating tenant checks across projection nodes cost more CPU vs a central authz cache?

Dario: tradeoff summary: early authz = less data downstream and fewer aggregates, but it complicates routing and increases memory pressure on projection nodes (policy cache).

Nina: also operational question — how do we handle canary/rollouts and policy changes for private deployments? different customers will want different guarantees.

Amal: rough sketch of flow:
```text
client -> ui-proxy -> projection-service (tenant filter + projection) -> query/model nodes
```
projection keeps a per-tenant policy cache, TTL ~30s.

Tess: TTL 30s seems risky for org membership changes; we need an invalidation hook from the auth service (webhook or pubsub).

Dario: agreed. add admit-cache + subscription invalidation. bigger concern: projection pre-filtering can harm cross-tenant batching opportunities — could raise p99.

Nina: right — batching across tenants is currently a major cost-saver. If projection segments requests by tenant we lose that. we need fallback strategies.

Amal: proposal refinement: projection does a soft-filter (marks rows that fail RBAC) and returns both payload + permission bits; query layer performs a final hard-recheck before emitting results. keeps batching intact.

Tess: soft-filter + recheck = extra hop/latency. we should quantify: median vs p99 impact. also check token/cost impact for hosted customers.

Dario: rough perf numbers from local microbench: recheck adds ~2–8ms median, ~15–30ms at p99 depending on payload size. if projection work is cheap (no heavy joins) median stays low.

Nina: operational complexity increases. ops wants a single audit trail for RBAC decisions. if split, ensure logs can be correlated (request id).

Amal: agreed — add structured RBAC headers and correlation: X-RB-Decision: allow|deny|soft-flag, X-RB-Request-ID, X-RB-Policy-Version.

ops-bot: deploy 1762345800: canary projection-service v1.2 started in us-west-2 :rocket:

Tess: noted. will run perf harness: 1k rps mixed-tenants, capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost.

Dario: also want a feature-flag to toggle per-route hard vs soft filtering so we can test per-customer config.

Nina: +1. enterprise/on-prem customers may require hard-filter-only. flag should be customer-scoped.

Amal: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with diagram, SLO impact table, audit header schema, and a rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> opt-in per-customer). i'll ping reviewers.

Tess: +1, ping me for perf validation.

Dario: i'll run batching-loss sims and validate KV cache interactions.

Nina: ops will confirm logging/trace correlation and invalidation hooks.

Amal: thanks — will post RFC in #eng-platform and link this thread for context.
